utterances.text: I truly cannot. I cannot tell you where the building was and what it looked like. It is in the centre of town, between Biogradska Street and onwards. But I really cannot mark it on the map, and the same goes for the police station as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Then, Mr. President, if we could have this exhibit marked and I tender it. And we will zoom in again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is it -- the whole presentation, I assume, is what is being tendered not just that page --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- with that marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that since the witness told us what locations were wrong or not recognised by him that we should at least know what he looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, we have now both his markings and the agenda which, as far as the testimony is concerned, are not or at least not to the knowledge of the witness accurate. That's all included in -- Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit D1446.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1446 is admitted into evidence. Could I ask you one additional question. What you marked as A, is that the same residential area you earlier marked as where you saw the shells falling --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Barice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. And then, Mr. Misetic, I see a yellow line with 50, is that a grid reference line?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, those are the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be easier if I gave you a blank map, which is, I believe, one back. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we blow this one up?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does that help you, Mr. Sinobad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I can do any better on this. I would still have to be speculating. I really can't tell where the municipal building is. It is probably close to the figure 49, but I only presume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me see if can I help you out what we believe some of the positions to be and maybe that will help to orient on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And can we go forward? Just keep moving through the exhibit and we'll get to the one that identifies all the buildings in the city and see if he can orient himself. Can we go to the next -- two slides forward, please. Okay. If we zoom out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Number 1 would be the bus station; 3, is where the municipal building is; 4 is the police station; number 5, that's -- should be a big visual anchor for you is the Macura barracks. So if you know where the Macura barracks are now on this overview, does that help you orient yourself on this map as to where, for example, the police station would be vis-a-vis the Macura barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If the police station is marked with 4, then I don't think that is the right location because it is too far from the street going through Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you think it is closer to the middle of this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At number 13, do you remember a -- a Catholic nuns' convent being at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no convent at the time. It was Our Lady's church there at the time, in the centre. And behind that there was a building with nuns and priests. And there was only a road between them and the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at 7, 8 and 9, do you recognise those at number 7 to be the Kepal factory, 8 to be the cold storage factory and 9 to be the winery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And number --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Along that route, along the road from the barracks through Benkovac and that's where you come across Kepal. The cold storage facility and the winery. I do think those could be the locations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At number 10 do you recognise that there was a hotel at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The hotel was not far from the bus station, some 50 metres away, up the hill. Of course, all this provided that 1 is indeed the bus station, then the number 10 would be the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could we go to the next slide, please. Again, these are some of the targets from the Jagoda list. If we could go to the next slide, please. The Chamber will note that we put the circles that Mr. Rajcic drew in Benkovac and overlayed them on this map to see the correspondence with what was on the target list as of the 30th of July, 1995. If we can go to the next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you mean the circles on the map or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Circles on the map that we just saw are taken from a map and -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I mean, Mr. Rajcic put them on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're all aware that these are no circles but ovals which of course is [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to make the following statement on behalf of the Chamber. It is the Chamber's statement concerning the Prosecution's submission of the Rule 92 ter statements for Witnesses 59, 60, 61, 62, and 63, who would give evidence about the recording of the soldier Brioni meeting of the 31st of July, 1995, as well as the transcription thereof, and the chain of custody of these records. These witnesses are on the Prosecution's witness list but until very recently the Prosecution had not decided whether these witnesses needed to be called or not. It is clear from the Prosecution's pre-trial brief that the Brioni meeting is of significance to the Prosecution's case. Both the Gotovina Defence and the Markac Defence have specifically challenged the authenticity of the records of this meeting in their pre-trial briefs but have not elaborated on those challenges. Apparently in response, the Prosecution presented an expert report of Peter French addressing, in the Chamber's provisional view, the most likely reasons for the Defence challenges to authenticity. After discussions between the parties, the Defence accepted the expert report and concluded that they did not need to cross-examine the expert. The Defence has, however, not stipulated to the authenticity of the records of the Brioni meeting. Whereas in most cases the production of an audio recording and a transcript thereof, as well as an expert report on technical aspects of the records would meet the burden of proof in relation to a conversation and its content, the Defence here apparently wants to reserve its position with regard to authenticity. One of the recently heard witnesses, Marko Rajcic, challenged the accuracy of the transcript. However, it remains to be determined whether the inconsistencies between the transcript and the witness's testimony are due to faulty memory of the witness, inaccurate transcript of the Brioni meeting, or any other factor. This said, the Chamber considers that particular circumstances may exist which could invalidate the convincing potential of the evidence presented by the Prosecution to date concerning the authenticity of the records of the Brioni meeting. The Chamber is uncertain whether such particular circumstances will be invoked by the Defence in support of any challenges it may make to authenticity or whether the Defence position is simply that the evidence presented is insufficient to reach a finding of satisfactory proof of authenticity. It appears as if the Prosecution's calling of further evidence on authenticity is triggered by the recent testimony of Marko Rajcic and the lack of insight into the nature of any challenges to authenticity that the Defence may later proffer. What the Prosecution apparently seeks to do is to remedy a challenge of unknown character by proposing evidence of Witnesses 59, 60, 61, 62, and 63. Under these circumstances, the Chamber considers that for the Prosecution to now attempt to provide a remedy for every possible later attack on the authenticity of the relevant material is an inefficient way of proceeding. The nature of any possible further challenges to authenticity is, at this moment, open to speculation. Accordingly, the Chamber is of the view that it would be a waste of resources for the Prosecution to attempt to anticipate such challenges by calling the five witnesses. This is particularly so if disclosure by the Defence of the nature of the challenges should call for a more focussed or a different approach. To present additional evidence on, for example, the chain of custody of the records when the Defence may have authenticity concerns totally foreign to that issue, goes directly against interests of judicial economy. In the absence of any indication that hearing the five witnesses will assist the Chamber in making its determination on matters in dispute, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to consider the withdrawal of their Rule 92 ter motions in relation to Witnesses 59, 60, 61, 62, and 63, despite the fact that the Prosecution has not as yet exhausted its allocated number of hours for the presentation of its case, as well as the fact that these witnesses are on the Prosecution's witness list. The situation described also has other procedural consequences. First, the Chamber will consider whether and in what way it may invite the Gotovina and Markac Defence to further clarify their positions in relation to the authenticity of the records of the Brioni meeting. Secondly, the Chamber informs the parties that the Chamber's current approach with regard to this issue will likely lead it to take a very liberal approach if the Prosecution, once knowing more about the nature of the authenticity concerns of the Defence, would seek to remedy those concerns at a later stage of the proceedings through these particular witnesses. Moreover, although the Chamber does not wish, at this moment, to further explore the question of the authenticity of the records of the Brioni meeting, the Chamber reminds the parties of the powers it has, pursuant to Rules 85(A) and 98, and the obligations of the Defence under Rule 65 ter. And this concludes the Chamber's statement on this matter. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 3rd of March, 9.00, Courtroom I.
